 MCSO: School bus driver taken to hospital after crash near intersection in Penfield
 PENFIELD, N.Y. — The Monroe County Sheriff’s Office said a Penfield school bus went off-road and crashed into a tree, leading to the bus driver going to the hospital.
 The driver was taken to the hospital for evaluation, and the bus aide and four students who were also involved in the crash were evaluated by EMS and didn’t go to the hospital, deputies said.
 The sheriff’s office said they responded to the crash, which was near the intersection of Pine Brook Circle and Penfield Road in Penfield, just before 3 p.m. on Friday.
 News10NBC’s Tom Kowalski went to the crash, he said the bus crashed into a tree on a home’s front lawn, and the airbags were deployed.
 Tom reported live from the scene after being there for about an hour. Parents in the area shared their reactions as they waited for their children to come home from school.
 Gregory Pennes said he has owned his house for two years and has already seen one crash come onto his property.
 “Couple months ago, there was a similar accident right at the intersection where a truck did about a 180 and hit the main pole for the light infrastructure. I have no idea how, but it’s another one that you walk out your front door and you kind of head scratch there for a second,” Pennes said.
 Across the street, Gina Grudier said she has had a similar experience.
 “Personally, we’ve lived at this place for three years and we have already had two cars go straight on Watson, where it stops and into our backyard. It’s really scary,” Grudier said.
 “I was filled with anxiety, fear and worry. When I saw it was a school bus I immediately started praying. I was waiting for my child to get home from school and she came in and let me know there were some parents parked in our driveway, and were up trying to get to their students,” said Grudier.
 The Penfield Central School District said it is planning its own investigation.
